title: Birds & Botanicals
description: The art of scientific observation — Audubon's birds and the great botanical plates.

items.title: Nocturne: Blue and Gold—Southampton Water
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas by James McNeill Whistler captures the tranquil expanse of Southampton Water under a moonlit or twilight sky. Through a masterful blend of blues and golds, Whistler transforms the landscape into an ethereal study of atmosphere and color harmony, emphasizing beauty over literal depiction.
items.tags: nocturne, seascape, aestheticism, atmospheric, tonalism, blue and gold, tranquility

items.title: At Mouquin's
items.description_narrative: William Glackens's 'At Mouquin's' captures a lively restaurant interior, depicting patrons engaged in dining and conversation. Rendered in oil on canvas, this 1905 work exemplifies a candid observation of urban life.
items.tags: restaurant, urban life, genre scene, american art, ashcan school, early 20th century, social realism

items.title: James William Wallack
items.description_narrative: This oil on canvas painting by Charles Robert Leslie depicts James William Wallack. Created between 1835 and 1840, it showcases Leslie's skill as a portraitist.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, 19th century, male figure, charles robert leslie, james william wallack, american art, british art

items.title: James Vibert, Sculptor
items.description_narrative: Ferdinand Hodler's 1907 oil on canvas presents a portrait titled 'James Vibert, Sculptor'. The painting depicts the sculptor James Vibert, created by Hodler, and serves as an example of his portraiture.
items.tags: portraiture, male subject, sculptor, oil painting, 1907, ferdinand hodler

items.title: The Fountain, Villa Torlonia, Frascati, Italy
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent captures the grand fountain at Villa Torlonia in Frascati, Italy. The artwork masterfully renders the play of light and shadow across the water and surrounding classical architecture.
items.tags: landscape, Italy, fountain, villa, oil painting, light, Edwardian, architecture

items.title: Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: This tempera on panel artwork, 'Scenes from the Life of Saint John the Baptist,' was created by Bartolomeo di Giovanni. Dating from around 1490–95, it vividly depicts significant moments from the saint's life.
items.tags: religious, narrative, early renaissance, italian, tempera, saint john the baptist

items.title: Stoke-by-Nayland
items.description_narrative: John Constable's "Stoke-by-Nayland" depicts a familiar rural English landscape, rendered with his characteristic attention to natural light and atmospheric conditions. This oil on canvas masterwork captures the vastness of the Suffolk countryside under a dynamic sky, reflecting Constable's deep connection to his native region.
items.tags: landscape, romanticism, england, nature, rural, atmospheric, 19th century

items.title: Landscape with Saint John on Patmos
items.description_narrative: Nicolas Poussin's "Landscape with Saint John on Patmos" depicts the evangelist on the island of Patmos, a traditional setting for the writing of the Book of Revelation. The scene is presented as an idealized classical landscape, reflecting Poussin's characteristic approach to integrating figures within grand, structured natural environments.
items.tags: landscape, religious, classical, baroque, serene, saint john, patmos

items.title: Mrs. George Swinton (Elizabeth Ebsworth)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's 1897 portrait of Mrs. George Swinton captures her elegant pose and sophisticated attire. This oil on canvas exemplifies Sargent's mastery of society portraiture and his distinctive brushwork.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, society portraiture, gilded age, elegance, late 19th century, realism, london society

items.title: The Captive Slave (Ira Aldridge)
items.description_narrative: This 1827 oil on canvas by John Philip Simpson portrays Ira Aldridge, an African American actor, in a poignant dramatic role as a captive slave. The artwork captures a moment of intense emotion, reflecting themes of bondage and human dignity.
items.tags: portrait, slavery, Ira Aldridge, acting, oil painting, 19th century, dramatic, realism

items.title: Rip Van Winkle
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts a scene from Washington Irving's classic American short story, 'Rip Van Winkle,' first published in 1819. John Quidor frequently drew inspiration from literary sources, bringing narrative depth to his canvases.
items.tags: american painting, romanticism, literature, folklore, narrative, oil painting

items.title: Coast Scene, Bathers
items.description_narrative: James McNeill Whistler's 'Coast Scene, Bathers' presents a tranquil view of figures along a shoreline. Executed in oil on panel, the work exemplifies his nuanced approach to color and atmosphere, capturing the subtle interplay of light and water.
items.tags: seascape, bathers, shoreline, tonalism, aestheticism, oil painting, 19th century, serene

items.title: Grey and Silver: Old Battersea Reach
items.description_narrative: This painting captures a serene view of the Thames at Battersea Reach, rendered in Whistler's characteristic muted tones of grey and silver. The work exemplifies his exploration of atmospheric effects and tonal harmony, reducing elements to evocative visual poetry.
items.tags: river scene, London, tonalism, aestheticism, urban landscape, boats, serene, subtle

items.title: The Artist in His Studio
items.medium: Oil on paper mounted on panel
items.description_narrative: James McNeill Whistler's 'The Artist in His Studio' offers an intimate glimpse into a painter's private creative space. Rendered in oil on paper mounted on panel, the work subtly reveals details of the artistic environment during the mid-19th century.
items.tags: artist, studio, interior, oil painting, 19th century, american art, british art

items.title: Mrs. John Nicholson (Hannah Duncan) and John Nicholson, Jr.
items.description_narrative: This double portrait by Charles Willson Peale depicts Hannah Duncan Nicholson and her son, John Nicholson, Jr., capturing a tender familial moment. Painted in oil on canvas in 1790, it exemplifies Peale's skill in rendering lifelike figures and intimate domestic scenes.
items.tags: portrait, mother and child, family, 18th century, american art, oil painting, realism, domestic scene

items.title: Arrangement in Flesh Color and Brown: Portrait of Arthur Jerome Eddy
items.description_narrative: This striking oil portrait, titled "Arrangement in Flesh Color and Brown," captures Arthur Jerome Eddy with an emphasis on color harmony rather than detailed representation. Created by James McNeill Whistler in 1894, it exemplifies his innovative approach to portraiture as a study in tonal relationships and artistic arrangement.
items.tags: portrait, oil painting, whistler, tonalism, aestheticism, fin de siècle, american art

items.title: Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre)
items.description_narrative: John Singer Sargent's oil on canvas portrait of Madame Paul Escudier (Louise Lefevre) captures the sitter with characteristic elegance and directness. Painted in 1882, the work exemplifies Sargent's mastery of light and texture in rendering a commanding social presence.
items.tags: portrait, woman, society portraiture, realism, elegant, 19th century, american art

items.title: Icebound
items.description_narrative: John Henry Twachtman's 'Icebound' captures a serene winter landscape, likely reflecting the artist's home in Greenwich, Connecticut. The composition features a muted palette and delicate brushwork, evoking the quiet beauty and reflective atmosphere of a snow-covered scene.
items.tags: winter, landscape, snow, ice, impressionism, american impressionism, serene, subtle
